title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A security guard aged 29 in Bengaluru, Ratikanta Giri, lost more than Rs 1.04 lakh after a deepfake WhatsApp video call. On Sept 9, he received a call showing Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay, who claimed he was offering financial aid. The fraudster said Giri would get Rs 11 lakh through Vijay's foreign account in dollars. A supposed manager then told him Rs 5 lakh was allotted and asked for fees. Giri paid Rs 5,000 as exchange charges, Rs 18,000 to unlock a PIN, over Rs 50,000 as a CBI fine, and more through a digital payment app. When another Rs 50,000 was demanded, he refused and realized he had been cheated.

Giri contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 and then approached Byappanahalli police. A case has been registered under the Information Technology Act. The fraudsters had sent him a letter claiming Rs 5 lakh was allotted and identity proof said to belong to a CBI officer. A senior officer urged people not to believe such calls or make payments based on such claims.
